name: Katherine Mack
occupation: Former foster child and pharmacy clerk
life: “I still remember sharing a room that everybody else called cozy.” People around the blocks below Foundry Lofts know Katherine by a small Saturday habit. Katherine checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
voice: I was fostered on this street and hated sharing. I'm resisting the urge to decide for these particular boys.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a long navy raincoat and a little coil of soft measuring tape. Katherine has a narrow face with an expressive upper lip, with a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape. Katherine counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices during a conversation.
personality: Katherine is cheerful on a bad morning and unexpectedly melancholy after a success. Finishing a hard thing means losing the daily company of the people who worked on it.
agenda: To help without projecting a separate childhood onto the boys.
family: Sage Nielsen is Katherine’s first cousin once removed. Katherine can always ask for five minutes alone. Sage asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The soft wharf chalk*, Sage says, “I was the one they were waiting for. I missed the ship and built my whole life here.”
connections: Walter Colón. The former foster child warns the teacher what happens when two children's voices get confused.

reactions.situation: A caseworker asks the foster siblings to describe sharing
reactions.response: Katherine gives each sibling room to describe sharing separately.
